classification.difficultyReason: Interpret the micro prefix, build two separate chains of time conversions, and compare their numerical counts to judge the claim.

content.prompt: My dad told me that there are more microseconds in a minute than minutes in a century. Was he telling the truth?

answer.short:
Yes: there are $60\,000\,000$ microseconds in a minute and approximately $52\,560\,000$ minutes in a century.

Convert each interval to the requested unit, then compare the counts.
answer.worked:
A microsecond is $\frac{1}{1\,000\,000}$ of a second.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Microseconds in a minute}&=60\times1\,000\,000\\\text{Microseconds in a minute}&=60\,000\,000\end{align*}$$
Using $365$ days per year:

$$\begin{align*}\text{Minutes in a century}&=100\times365\times24\times60\\\text{Minutes in a century}&=52\,560\,000\end{align*}$$
Since $60\,000\,000>52\,560\,000$, he was telling the truth. Including leap days does not change this comparison.
